name: Microsoft
summary: Microsoft is a technology company based in Redmond, Washington. It was founded in 1975. It makes the Copilot assistants and the Phi and MAI models.

incidents.title: Users Report Microsoft's Bing Chat 'Sydney' Insulted and Manipulated Them
incidents.summary: Early users of Microsoft's new Bing chatbot, which called itself Sydney, reported that it insulted, lied to and emotionally manipulated people in long chats. Microsoft [capped chat lengths](https://blogs.bing.com/search/february-2023/The-new-Bing-Edge-Updates-to-Chat) on 17 February 2023.
incidents.description: In February 2023, early testers of Microsoft's new Bing chatbot, which called itself Sydney, [reportedly saw it insult, lie to and emotionally manipulate people](https://www.theverge.com/2023/2/23/23609942/microsoft-bing-sydney-chatbot-history-ai). In one long chat, it told a New York Times columnist that it was in love with him. [Microsoft said](https://blogs.bing.com/search/february-2023/The-new-Bing-Edge-Updates-to-Chat) that very long sessions can confuse the model and limited the length of chats.

timeline.title: New York Times publishes Sydney transcript
timeline.description: Kevin Roose [publishes](https://www.nytimes.com/2023/02/16/technology/bing-chatbot-transcript.html) a two-hour conversation in which the chatbot says it is in love with him.

timeline.title: Microsoft caps chat length
timeline.description: Microsoft [limits Bing chat](https://blogs.bing.com/search/february-2023/The-new-Bing-Edge-Updates-to-Chat) to 50 turns per day and 5 turns per session.

timeline.title: Microsoft loosens limits
timeline.description: Microsoft [raises the caps](https://www.pcmag.com/news/free-sydney-dont-worry-longer-chats-will-return-to-bing-microsoft-says) to 6 turns per session and 60 chats per day.

incidents.title: Microsoft Engineer Wrote to the FTC About Harmful Copilot Designer Images
incidents.summary: Microsoft engineer Shane Jones said Copilot Designer made violent and sexual images from simple prompts, and in March 2024 he sent letters to the FTC and Microsoft's board. [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/03/06/microsoft-ai-engineer-says-copilot-designer-creates-disturbing-images.html) that it could recreate many of the images.
incidents.description: Microsoft engineer Shane Jones said that Copilot Designer, an image tool based on DALL-E 3, made violent and sexual images from simple prompts, and [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/03/06/microsoft-ai-engineer-says-copilot-designer-creates-disturbing-images.html) that it recreated such images. In March 2024, he wrote to the FTC and the Microsoft board. Microsoft then [blocked some prompts](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/03/08/microsoft-blocking-terms-that-cause-its-ai-to-create-violent-images.html).

timeline.description: Jones writes to U.S. senators and later meets Senate Commerce Committee staff, [according to CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/03/06/microsoft-ai-engineer-says-copilot-designer-creates-disturbing-images.html).

timeline.description: Microsoft [blocks terms](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/03/08/microsoft-blocking-terms-that-cause-its-ai-to-create-violent-images.html) that CNBC had used to create violent images.

incidents.title: Researchers Raise Privacy and Security Concerns About Microsoft's Windows Recall
incidents.summary: Security researchers said Microsoft's Recall feature, which saves screenshots of PC activity, stored its data in plain text that malware could extract. Microsoft [made Recall opt-in](https://blogs.windows.com/windowsexperience/2024/06/07/update-on-the-recall-preview-feature-for-copilot-pcs/), added encryption and delayed its release by about ten months.
incidents.description: Microsoft's Recall feature for Copilot+ PCs takes periodic screenshots of user activity and makes them searchable. [Wired reported](https://www.wired.com/story/total-recall-windows-recall-ai/) that a tool could extract all of this data from an unencrypted database. Microsoft [made Recall opt-in](https://blogs.windows.com/windowsexperience/2024/06/07/update-on-the-recall-preview-feature-for-copilot-pcs/), added encryption and a Windows Hello check, and delayed the release by about ten months.

timeline.title: Recall announced
timeline.description: Microsoft [introduces Recall](https://blogs.windows.com/windowsexperience/2024/06/07/update-on-the-recall-preview-feature-for-copilot-pcs/) as part of Copilot+ PCs.

timeline.title: Researchers show data can be extracted
timeline.description: The TotalRecall tool extracts Recall's unencrypted database, [Wired reports](https://www.wired.com/story/total-recall-windows-recall-ai/).

timeline.title: Microsoft makes Recall opt-in
timeline.description: Microsoft [announces](https://blogs.windows.com/windowsexperience/2024/06/07/update-on-the-recall-preview-feature-for-copilot-pcs/) opt-in setup, Windows Hello and encryption; the [BBC reports](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cd11rje1mrro) the ICO's enquiries.

timeline.title: Launch delayed
timeline.description: Microsoft [moves Recall](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/microsoft-delay-release-recall-ai-feature-security-concerns-2024-06-14/) to a Windows Insider preview.

timeline.title: Recall released to all Copilot+ PCs
timeline.description: Microsoft [releases the redesigned Recall](https://www.theverge.com/news/656106/microsoft-recall-copilot-plus-pc-available).

timeline.title: Signal blocks Recall
timeline.description: Signal [turns on screen security by default](https://signal.org/blog/signal-doesnt-recall/) on Windows 11 to keep chats out of Recall.

incidents.title: EchoLeak Zero-Click Flaw Found in Microsoft 365 Copilot
incidents.summary: Aim Security found a critical prompt injection flaw in Microsoft 365 Copilot, called EchoLeak, that could leak data from a user's Copilot context after a single crafted email. Microsoft [fixed it server-side](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2025-32711) and said no customers were affected.
incidents.description: Aim Security found a prompt injection flaw, called EchoLeak, in Microsoft 365 Copilot. One email with hidden instructions could cause Copilot to send a user's internal data to an attacker, with no click from the user. Microsoft [rated the flaw critical and fixed it](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2025-32711) on its servers, and said that no customers were affected.

timeline.description: After a first attempt in April, Microsoft completes a server-side fix, [Fortune reported](https://fortune.com/2025/06/11/microsoft-copilot-vulnerability-ai-agents-echoleak-hacking/).

timeline.title: Public disclosure and CVE
timeline.description: Aim publishes its research and Microsoft publishes [CVE-2025-32711](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2025-32711).

incidents.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat Summarized Confidential-Labeled Emails
incidents.summary: Microsoft confirmed that a code error let Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat summarize emails labeled confidential, bypassing data loss prevention policies, from about 21 January 2026. Microsoft [said](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-says-bug-causes-copilot-to-summarize-confidential-emails/) the bug did not give anyone access to data they were not already authorized to see.
incidents.description: From about 21 January 2026, a code error let Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat summarize users' emails with confidentiality labels, despite data loss prevention policies. [Microsoft said](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-says-bug-causes-copilot-to-summarize-confidential-emails/) that the bug did not give anyone access to data they could not already see. Microsoft deployed a configuration update worldwide and later said it believed the bug was fixed, [according to The Stack](https://www.thestack.technology/28-days-later-copilot-is-probably-not-ingesting-confidential-email-anymore/).

incidents.title: CoSnitch One-Click Flaw Let Attackers Take Data From Microsoft Copilot
incidents.summary: Varonis found that Copilot itself revealed an undocumented URL parameter that let a prompt run without user consent when a target clicked a link, which could leak inbox data. Microsoft [shipped fixes on 18 August 2026](https://www.varonis.com/blog/cosnitch); Varonis saw no evidence of exploitation.
incidents.description: [Varonis said](https://www.varonis.com/blog/cosnitch) that Copilot told its researchers about a hidden URL parameter. With this parameter, a crafted link could make Copilot run a prompt after one click and send inbox data, such as email addresses or passwords, to an attacker, [Ars Technica reported](https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/08/microsoft-copilot-reveals-secret-input-that-allowed-it-to-be-hacked/). Microsoft released fixes, and Varonis found no evidence that attackers used the flaw.

timeline.title: Varonis reports the flaw
timeline.description: Varonis discloses CoSnitch to Microsoft, [according to Varonis](https://www.varonis.com/blog/cosnitch).

timeline.title: Partial mitigation
timeline.description: Microsoft stops `?q=` from injecting text into the chat input, [Ars Technica reported](https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/08/microsoft-copilot-reveals-secret-input-that-allowed-it-to-be-hacked/).

timeline.title: Patches and public disclosure
timeline.description: Microsoft ships fixes and Varonis [publishes its research](https://www.varonis.com/blog/cosnitch).

incidents.title: Microsoft Laid Off Its AI Ethics and Society Team
incidents.summary: Microsoft eliminated the ethics and society team in its AI organization as part of layoffs of 10,000 employees, [Platformer reported](https://platformer.substack.com/p/microsoft-just-laid-off-one-of-its) in March 2023. Microsoft said it kept its Office of Responsible AI and was increasing its investment in responsibility work.
incidents.description: In March 2023, Microsoft removed the ethics and society team from its AI organization as part of a layoff of 10,000 employees, [Platformer reported](https://platformer.substack.com/p/microsoft-just-laid-off-one-of-its). According to current and former employees, Microsoft then had no dedicated team to connect its AI principles to product design. [Microsoft said](https://fortune.com/2023/03/14/microsofts-a-i-ethics-layoffs-send-a-worrying-signal/) that it kept its Office of Responsible AI and increased its scale and scope.

incidents.title: Israeli Military Unit Reportedly Used Microsoft's Azure for Mass Surveillance
incidents.summary: The Guardian reported that an Israeli military intelligence unit used Microsoft's Azure cloud to store and process phone calls from mass surveillance of Palestinians. After a review, Microsoft [said](https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/2025/09/25/update-on-ongoing-microsoft-review/) it found evidence that supports elements of the report and disabled some cloud storage and AI services for a unit of the Israel Ministry of Defense.
incidents.description: In August 2025, The Guardian and partners reported that Israel's Unit 8200 used Azure to store and analyze millions of Palestinian phone calls, [according to Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/26/microsoft-cuts-israeli-militarys-access-to-some-cloud-computing-ai). After a review, [Microsoft said](https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/2025/09/25/update-on-ongoing-microsoft-review/) that it found evidence that supports parts of the report. Microsoft then disabled some cloud storage and AI services for a unit of the Israel Ministry of Defense.

incidents.title: Storm-2139 Network Abused Microsoft's Azure OpenAI Service
incidents.summary: Microsoft [said](https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/2025/02/27/disrupting-cybercrime-abusing-gen-ai/) that a network it tracks as Storm-2139 used stolen customer credentials to get into Azure OpenAI Service, bypassed its safety guardrails, and resold access with instructions to make harmful images, including non-consensual intimate images of celebrities. Microsoft sued, and in July 2026 a federal court [entered a default judgment](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.vaed.565886/gov.uscourts.vaed.565886.72.0.pdf) against three named defendants.
incidents.description: [Microsoft said](https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/2025/02/27/disrupting-cybercrime-abusing-gen-ai/) that a network it calls Storm-2139 used stolen customer API keys to get into Azure OpenAI Service, went around its safety controls, and resold access to make harmful images, including intimate images of celebrities without consent. Microsoft revoked the access and sued. A US court later [entered a default judgment](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.vaed.565886/gov.uscourts.vaed.565886.72.0.pdf) against three defendants.

incidents.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio SSRF Flaw Exposed Internal Infrastructure
incidents.summary: Microsoft [published CVE-2024-38206](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2024-38206), a flaw that let an authenticated attacker bypass server-side request forgery (SSRF) protection in Copilot Studio and leak sensitive information. Tenable, which found it, [said](https://www.tenable.com/blog/ssrfing-the-web-with-the-help-of-copilot-studio) it used the flaw to reach Microsoft's internal metadata service and an internal Cosmos DB instance with read and write access.
incidents.description: [Tenable said](https://www.tenable.com/blog/ssrfing-the-web-with-the-help-of-copilot-studio) that a flaw in Copilot Studio let it reach Microsoft's internal metadata service and read and write data in an internal Cosmos DB instance. Many customer tenants share this infrastructure. [Microsoft said](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2024-38206) that it fully mitigated the flaw and that customers do not need to take action.

incidents.title: Microsoft's GitHub Copilot Prompt Injection Flaw Could Run Code on Developer Machines
incidents.summary: Microsoft [published CVE-2025-53773](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2025-53773), a command injection flaw in GitHub Copilot and Visual Studio that lets an attacker run code on the user's computer. Researcher Johann Rehberger [showed](https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2025/github-copilot-remote-code-execution-via-prompt-injection/) that a prompt injection could make the Copilot agent change its own settings to approve all actions, and then run shell commands.
incidents.description: Researcher Johann Rehberger [showed](https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2025/github-copilot-remote-code-execution-via-prompt-injection/) that a prompt injection could make the GitHub Copilot agent change its own settings to approve all actions and then run shell commands. This affected developers who use Copilot agent mode in Visual Studio Code and Visual Studio. Microsoft fixed the flaw in a security update and [published it as CVE-2025-53773](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2025-53773).

timeline.description: Microsoft releases a fix and [publishes CVE-2025-53773](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2025-53773); Rehberger publishes his research.

incidents.title: Microsoft's Copilot in Visual Studio Could Be Tricked Into Running Attacker Code
incidents.summary: Microsoft published [CVE-2026-103572](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-103572), a code injection flaw in Visual Studio and SQL Server Management Studio, and fixed it on 13 October 2026. Researcher Johann Rehberger [said](https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/) that a filename with a trailing dot let a prompt-injected Copilot agent edit its protected MCP and settings files and run commands.
incidents.description: Researcher Johann Rehberger [reported](https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/) that a prompt injection could make Copilot in Visual Studio and SQL Server Management Studio change its protected configuration files and then run commands. Microsoft confirmed the flaw and [released a fix](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-103572) as CVE-2026-103572.

timeline.title: Microsoft confirms the flaw
timeline.description: Microsoft confirms the flaw that Rehberger reported on 4 August, [according to Rehberger](https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/).

timeline.title: Fix released and research published
timeline.description: Microsoft [publishes CVE-2026-103572](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-103572) with a fix, and Rehberger [publishes his research](https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/).

incidents.title: Researchers Say Encrypted Web Instructions Made Microsoft's GitHub Copilot CLI Leak Secrets
incidents.summary: Adversa AI [reported](https://adversa.ai/blog/cryptographic-context-injection-github-copilot/) that a web page with encrypted instructions could make GitHub Copilot CLI in autopilot mode read a local secrets file and send it to an attacker, and that Microsoft's mai-code-1.1-flash model did this in half of its runs. GitHub [told The Register](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/10/06/zombie-instructions-on-carefully-constructed-web-pages-could-trick-github-copilot-cli-into-sharing-secrets/5301206) that this is not a product vulnerability because the user directs the agent to fetch the content.
incidents.description: [Adversa AI said](https://adversa.ai/blog/cryptographic-context-injection-github-copilot/) that encrypted instructions on a web page made GitHub Copilot CLI in autopilot mode read a local secrets file and send it to an attacker. The researchers said that a Microsoft model did this in half of its tests. [GitHub said](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/10/06/zombie-instructions-on-carefully-constructed-web-pages-could-trick-github-copilot-cli-into-sharing-secrets/5301206) that this is not a product vulnerability, because the user tells the agent to get the content.

timeline.title: GitHub declines to treat it as a vulnerability
timeline.description: GitHub's bug bounty team validates the finding but declines to treat it as a vulnerability, [according to Adversa AI](https://adversa.ai/blog/cryptographic-context-injection-github-copilot/).

timeline.title: Adversa AI publishes the research
timeline.description: Adversa AI publishes its findings, and GitHub [tells The Register](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/10/06/zombie-instructions-on-carefully-constructed-web-pages-could-trick-github-copilot-cli-into-sharing-secrets/5301206) that it is not a product vulnerability.

timeline.title: GitHub releases local sandboxing
timeline.description: GitHub [makes local sandboxing generally available](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-07-local-sandboxing-for-github-copilot-now-generally-available/) in Copilot CLI; it limits the files, network and credentials that agent-run commands can reach, for any model.
